title: Batch Guardian: continuous batching recommender with profile drift detection
creator: Ethan Park
body: Build 'Batch Guardian', a continuous batching recommendation engine that profiles per-route and per-customer workloads, generates safe batching/caching configuration candidates, and applies them with automated metric-gated rollouts and fast rollback. This ticket covers the core recommender logic, safety checks, simulated dry-run evaluation, and first internal canary. The goal is to reduce per-token serving cost by safely increasing batching and enabling prefix/KV caching where appropriate while preventing SLO regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces configuration candidates (max_batch_ms, max_batch_size, target_utilization, kv_cache_enabled, kv_cache_ttl) for >90% of eligible routes
Predicted cost savings estimate provided for each candidate and matches offline simulation within +/-12%
Automated canary workflow applies a single-route candidate to 1% traffic, monitors gating metrics for 30 minutes, and automatically rolls back if any gating rule is violated
No route experiences >5% increase in p95 or >2% increase in error rate during canary for accepted candidates
Telemetry emits the drift_score and suggestion_reason for every evaluated route
Runbook documented and internal alpha rollout completed with at least 2 internal teams testing
technical_design: Overview: the recommender runs as a nightly job plus event-driven triggers for sudden workload changes. Inputs: per-route request traces (latency, seq_len, token_count), KV cache hit/miss, model time-per-token profiles, hardware characteristics, and quota/priority metadata.

Profiling: build a compact workload signature per route using histogram sketches for sequence length, inter-arrival times, and prefix similarity scores. Compute a drift_score by comparing current signature to the rolling 7-day baseline using cosine similarity + cumulative KL divergence.
Clustering: use an online micro-clustering step to group routes with similar signatures so recommendations can reuse candidate generation and reduce noise for low-traffic routes.

Candidate generation: heuristics produce discrete candidate sets parameterized by max_batch_ms, max_batch_size, target_utilization, kv_cache_enabled, kv_cache_ttl, and prefill_threshold. Use conservative defaults and progressive aggressiveness tiers.

Cost-latency simulator: lightweight simulator estimates token-cost and tail-latency impact of each candidate using sampled traces and model GPU throughput curves. Simulator accounts for KV cache hit-rate delta and batch packing inefficiencies.

Safety checks: apply a layered gate: static rule checks (SLO/policy hard limits), simulator pass (must not exceed p95 budget), and a canary gating plan. Generate human-readable failure reasons for auditability.

Apply flow: the recommender writes suggested config objects to the config store in a dormant state. An orchestration component performs transactional canary applies with metric hooks and rollback tokens. Applies are idempotent and revertible.

Rollback strategy: automatic rollback triggered by metric gates (latency, error rate, downstream timeouts) or by manual operator action. Support fast revert that restores previous config and triggers an alert with full diff and the simulator result used.

Drift detector: continuous monitoring that re-evaluates live routes and marks suggestions stale when drift_score exceeds threshold; stale suggestions are deprioritized and optionally rolled back if they were auto-applied.
Data retention & privacy: only ingest anonymized request-level features; no customer PII leaves the telemetry pipeline. Follow existing KMS policies for config storage encryption.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal only. Nightly run writes suggestions to config store; ops manually approves canary apply for 2 internal services. Runbook walkthrough and incident simulation included.

Beta: automated 1% traffic canary for opt-in customers for 2 weeks. Monitor gating metrics and collect cost/latency comparisons. If success rate >80% and SLO regressions <2% across samples, expand to 10%.

Full rollout: auto-suggest enabled for all eligible routes with operator review mailbox. Gradual ramp with automatic progressive increase in traffic percentage on stable metrics and delayed promotion to global config.
Emergency rollback: preconfigured 'panic' endpoint to revert all last-24hr Batch Guardian applies; retained previous configs for up to 7 days for quick restores.
telemetry_requirements: Emit 'batching.recommender.suggestion' events with route, suggestion_id, candidate_params, predicted_cost_delta, and reason_codes

Metrics: serving.latency.p50/p95/p99 (route), serving.error_rate (route), cost.per_token (route), kv_cache.hit_rate (route), drift_score (route), canary.apply_success (bool), canary.rollback_trigger_reason (tagged)
Dashboards: per-route suggestion history, predicted vs actual cost delta, canary outcomes, and global trend of accepted suggestions vs regressions
Alerts: page on canary rollback for production routes and on algorithm anomalies (e.g., sudden surge in rejected suggestions or model throughput mismatch)
Logs: include simulator inputs, sampled request IDs (anonymized), and pre/post config diffs for audit in a searchable store for 30 days
experiment_plan: Phase 1 (offline validation): run recommender in dry-run for 2 weeks across top 200 routes and compare simulator predictions to actual observed cost/latency with existing configs
Phase 2 (internal canary): apply to 2 internal services with manual rollback enabled, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, refine heuristics and conservative thresholds
Phase 3 (customer beta): invite 5 customers to opt-in for automated 1% canaries, measure cumulative cost savings and SLO delta for 30 days
Success metrics: mean cost reduction per-route >8%, median p95 latency change <= +2%, and overall rollback rate <5% for accepted suggestions
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Raman: Spiked the initial profiler code and uploaded sample signatures. Found that low-traffic routes need micro-clustering to avoid noisy suggestions.
2026-02-18 - Connor Li: Reviewed candidate generation heuristics. Suggested adding prefill_threshold and a tiered aggressiveness score to reduce oscillation.
2026-02-25 - Marta Velasquez (PM): Approved metrics set. Please ensure drift_score is exposed to customers in the console so they can opt-out when needed.
2026-03-03 - Engineering review: Simulated runs on G4 cluster show predicted cost delta matches observed within 10% for high-traffic routes; low-traffic variance still high.
2026-03-08 - Security: Confirmed no PII in profiler payloads; KV config payloads must be encrypted at rest.
